Subject: Post-call: PayGrid model fit / next steps & parity thresholds

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side after the discovery:

Summary from the call:
- Primary use case: real-time invoice understanding (line-item extraction + payment terms classification) integrated into PayGrid's payments workflow.
- Target latency: 150ms p95 for single-request inference in the Dedicated environment.
- Primary quality metric: entity extraction F1 (weighted towards precision) and classification accuracy on a 12k prompt test set.
- Current in-house baseline: closed/proprietary model tuned by PayGrid (we discussed aiming for parity or better on F1).

What we’re attaching:
- paygrid_eval_promptset_v1.csv — representative prompt sets from your prod anonymized dataset (12k rows).
- benchmark_results_open_vs_baseline.pdf — our initial benchmark template and fields we’ll populate.

Recommended evaluation plan (proposed):
1) Redwood runs a 2-week eval comparing the following candidates: Llama2-Chat-70B (instruction-tuned), Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-40B-Instruct (quantized where appropriate).
2) Run identical prompt set (attached) and measure: extraction F1, classification accuracy, hallucination rate on a 1k holdout, and p95 latency on a Dedicated staging GPU pool.
3) Acceptance threshold options (please confirm which you prefer):
   a) Strict parity: open model >= baseline F1 and >= baseline accuracy; latency within 1.5x baseline.
   b) Quality-first: open model >= 0.98 * baseline F1 with latency and cost advantages.

Next steps we need from you:
- Confirm which acceptance threshold (a or b) you want to use as the go/no-go.
- Confirm a test window for Redwood to run the eval (we can start as soon as we have a signed NDA for the eval data).
- Any additional success metrics we should add (e.g., token-level confidence, specific error classes).

I’ve looped in Aditya (SE) and Dylan (CS) who will own the evaluation run and kernel/quantization tuning.

Thanks —

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the acceptance criteria: 

1) Baseline numbers: we can share current baseline metrics but want to anonymize some of the client-sensitive examples. Baseline on our 12k set is: extraction F1 = 0.862, classification accuracy = 0.912. Latency p95 on our infra averages ~120ms.

2) Acceptance preference: our product team prefers option (b) (quality-first) unless Redwood can show substantial cost/latency wins without loss in critical edge cases. For us, minimizing false positives on invoice line extraction is important (precision target >= 0.85).

3) Data sharing / NDA: we’re happy to proceed under a short eval NDA. Can you share Redwood’s standard eval NDA?

4) Timing: we want to kick off the eval in the week of Apr 12 if feasible. We’ll also want a short sync with the SE once you have the staging environment configured.

Appreciate the attachments. A couple of asks: include a brief column in the CSV that maps to our internal labels (anonymized token IDs) and confirm you won’t retain raw text beyond the eval window.

Best,

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks — quick technical notes from the SE side to set expectations before the eval: 

Models we recommend for the evaluation (balanced across cost/quality):
- Llama2-Chat-70B (instruction-tuned): strong extraction quality, larger memory/KV needs.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct: good middle ground for entity tasks when quantized (8-bit/4-bit).
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: cost-efficient, often surprisingly competitive on classification tasks.

What we’ll measure and our blind-controlled setup:
- Exact-match and F1 for extraction; macro/micro F1 for multi-label classification; precision on top-k entities to capture false positives.
- Hallucination rate measured by a small oracle set (50 manually labeled edge cases).
- Latency measured on Dedicated staging (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) with realistic batch shaping; we’ll provide p50/p95/p99.
- Cost estimate: token-level cost projection normalized to your traffic pattern (we’ll surface $/1M tokens for each model/quantization).

On parity and acceptance:
- For parity we recommend a two-tier pass:
   1) Quality gate: open model >= 0.98 * baseline F1 AND precision >= 0.85 on edge cases.
   2) Ops gate: p95 latency <= 1.5x baseline OR clear cost reduction > 20%.
- If a model passes quality but misses ops, we can explore model distillation / quantization strategies or a hybrid routing approach (fast small model for clear cases, large model for ambiguous).

Data handling and retention:
- We will run the eval in your VPC or Redwood Private staging if you prefer; otherwise, we’ll sign an eval NDA and run in a segregated staging tenant. We will not retain raw prompts beyond 30 days post-eval unless you opt-in.

Next steps I’ll take if you confirm Apr 12 start:
- Provision a 3-node Dedicated staging pool and pre-load quantized kernels.
- Run a 10k-run smoke test and share the evaluation dashboard link.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
